caption:
### Global Metadata

Basic Attributes: bpm is 84. key is G, and scale is minor. Victorian Chamber Noir / Procedural Mystery Score - string quartet and pump organ, not hybrid trailer orchestra.

Global Emotional Progression: It begins as a cold intellectual exercise, a single violin figure stated plainly, unhurried, curious rather than frightened - the sound of a man enjoying a problem. Through the middle it hardens: the figure is answered by lower strings that will not let it go, and what was a puzzle becomes a pursuit. At two-thirds the ground changes entirely - the room falls away and the piece opens into dry sunlit emptiness, no walls, no reverb, a wronged man's grief held on one open fifth. From there it accelerates as revenge, the violin figure returning at double speed and an octave down, until it is stopped mid-phrase.

Application Scenarios & Imagery: a gaslit London room at three in the morning, a magnifying glass over a smear of blood on plaster, hansom wheels on wet cobbles, and then an alkali plain at noon with two figures and a hundred miles of nothing.

Sonics & Production Profile: mid-forward and close, a small dry room with rosin and bow noise audible, the low end from a double bass and a foot-pumped harmonium rather than synthetic sub, almost no reverb tail in the second half.

### Vocal Details

This piece is instrumental. The lead is a solo violin played in the drawing-room manner, the instrument the detective himself owns.

### Arrangement

Instrument Lifecycle. Primary: a solo violin played in the drawing-room manner, the instrument the detective himself owns. Secondary: cello and double bass entering as a walking pizzicato pulse beneath the second statement; a prepared piano with paper on the strings answering in the middle; a lone open-fifth fiddle drone replacing the room entirely at the turn to the plain.

Groove & Foundation Progression: no drum kit and no taiko at any point; the pulse is a walking double bass and a pocket watch, struck objects only. The pulse doubles once at the turn and again into the final wave, then stops dead on a downbeat.

Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: a new colour introduced before each restatement of the figure; one beat of total silence before the last impact; the piece ends on a single low note left to die in the room. The density of events rises steadily through the final third so that the last quarter carries the most attacks of the whole piece, then stops.
